requirements: Reproduce the core contributions of vLLM/PagedAttention: an attention algorithm that stores KV cache in non-contiguous paged memory blocks, a serving engine built on top of it, and demonstrated 2-4× throughput improvements over FasterTransformer and Orca on OPT/LLaMA models across ShareGPT/Alpaca/WMT16 workloads.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PagedAttention kernel is implemented per Section 4.1 / Eq. 5: KV cache is partitioned into fixed-size KV blocks, the kernel fetches non-contiguous blocks via a block table, and computes attention block-wise as illustrated in Figure 5.
The PagedAttention algorithm is specified per Section 4.1: KV cache is partitioned into fixed-size KV blocks of block size B, and the block-wise attention computation follows Eq. 5.

Code has been implemented that partitions per-sequence KV cache into fixed-size KV blocks, each holding B tokens' key vectors K_j = (k_{(j-1)B+1}, ..., k_{jB}) and value vectors V_j = (v_{(j-1)B+1}, ..., v_{jB}), where B is a configurable block-size parameter.

verification.spec: Inspect the KV cache/block manager module. Verify: (1) a KV-block class/struct exists with a configurable block_size parameter B, (2) instantiating with B=16 produces blocks that hold exactly 16 token slots for keys and 16 for values, (3) instantiating with B=8 and B=32 also works and produces correspondingly sized blocks, (4) a sequence of length L=50 tokens partitioned with B=16 produces ceil(50/16)=4 logical blocks, with the last block partially filled, (5) block indexing satisfies K_j covering tokens (j-1)*B+1 .. j*B.

sub_tasks.requirements: The KV-block layout uses per-head, per-layer separate block tables (as chosen in the paper's footnote 1), so each attention head at each layer has its own key/value block storage rather than a single interleaved block table.

verification.spec: Inspect the KV cache allocator/block manager. Verify: (1) block storage is dimensioned such that separate physical blocks (or separate block-table entries) exist per (layer, head) rather than a single interleaved block holding all layers/heads, (2) for a model with num_layers=L and num_heads=H, the block allocator's per-block tensor shape or block-table structure exposes L and H as separate dimensions (e.g., allocated GPU tensor has shape [num_blocks, num_layers, num_heads, block_size, head_dim] or blocks are indexed by (layer, head) keys), (3) writing to head h at layer l does not touch storage for head h' or layer l'.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes attention block-wise per Eq. 5: for each block j the kernel produces A_{ij} = exp(q_i^T K_j / sqrt(d)) / sum_t exp(q_i^T k_t / sqrt(d)) and accumulates o_i = sum_j V_j A_{ij}^T.

verification.spec: Locate the PagedAttention kernel/reference implementation in src/. Construct a test harness that invokes the attention op with known q, K, V blocks and inspects intermediate tensors (or checks that the numerical output equals torch's softmax(q K^T / sqrt(d)) V computed block-wise via Eq. 5). Verify that per-block A_ij is computed as normalized softmax over the full context and o_i is the sum over blocks of V_j A_ij^T.

sub_tasks.requirements: The block-wise softmax normalization uses a global denominator over all blocks j (sum_t exp(q_i^T k_t / sqrt(d))) rather than per-block local softmax, matching Eq. 5's row-vector A_{ij} definition.

verification.spec: Feed a case where per-block max logits differ significantly across blocks (e.g., artificially large logits in block 0, small in block 1). Compare kernel output to (a) a global-softmax reference (correct) and (b) a per-block local-softmax reference (incorrect). Assert kernel matches (a) within 1e-2 fp16 tolerance and does NOT match (b) beyond 1e-2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel applies the same causal masking as standard self-attention (Eq. 4): tokens at positions > i are not attended to, and the last partially-filled block only uses its actually-filled positions.

verification.spec: For a single query position i with context_len = L (where L is not a multiple of block_size), run the PagedAttention kernel and compare to torch reference softmax(q_i K[:L]^T / sqrt(d)) V[:L]. Then modify K/V positions L..end (beyond the filled prefix) with random noise; assert the kernel output is unchanged, proving positions > i (and unfilled slots in the last block) are masked out.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PagedAttention kernel fetches KV blocks non-contiguously in physical memory via the per-request block table, matching Figure 5's illustration.

Code has been implemented such that the kernel accepts a block-table tensor (mapping logical block index -> physical block id) and reads each block's keys/values from the physical address indicated by the table rather than assuming contiguity.

verification.spec: Inspect the PagedAttention kernel signature; ensure it accepts a block_table tensor (int, shape [num_seqs, max_num_blocks_per_seq]) as an argument. Then run the kernel with a physically-scrambled block layout — allocate a contiguous KV pool but place logical blocks 0,1,2 at non-adjacent physical block ids via the block_table — and verify output equals a reference contiguous-KV attention on the same logical sequence.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel accepts a per-sequence context length (or number-of-filled-positions) input so that the last logical block is only read up to its filled slot count, and positions beyond are excluded from the softmax.

verification.spec: Inspect kernel signature and verify it accepts a context_lens (int32) tensor. Then set context_len = 5 with block_size = 4 (so last block has 1 filled slot); fill unfilled slots of the last block with NaN. Run the kernel and assert output is finite and equals reference over the first 5 K/V positions, proving unfilled slots are excluded from softmax.

sub_tasks.requirements: Kernel behavior: given a query vector q_i and a block table pointing to three non-contiguous physical KV blocks (as in Figure 5), the kernel correctly reads each block by dereferencing the block-table entry (verified by a unit test that scrambles physical block order and checks output invariance).

verification.spec: Reproduce Fig. 5's example: 3 KV blocks stored at non-contiguous physical indices (e.g., [4, 0, 7]). Run PagedAttention with block_table = [4, 0, 7] and compare against reference attention over the logical concatenation. Then shuffle the physical block indices to [7, 4, 0] with data moved accordingly and block_table updated to [0, 2, 1] (mapping to new physical locations); assert output is identical to first configuration within 1e-3 fp16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Kernel behavior: a unit test that permutes the physical block IDs (holding logical order fixed via the block table) produces bitwise-identical (or within-fp16-tolerance) attention outputs, demonstrating true non-contiguous access.

verification.spec: Run PagedAttention with block_table [0,1,2,3] on physical blocks containing K/V data. Apply a random permutation pi to physical blocks (physically move data) and set block_table to pi so logical order is preserved. Assert the two outputs match within 1e-3 fp16 absolute tolerance across all query positions, proving true non-contiguous access via block_table indirection.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PagedAttention kernel is numerically equivalent to standard self-attention on the same underlying KV sequence, so replacing standard attention with PagedAttention preserves model outputs.

Unit test: for a single-head, single-request case with context length exactly equal to block_size, the PagedAttention output matches a reference torch attention (softmax(qK^T/sqrt(d))V) within 1e-3 absolute tolerance in fp16.

verification.spec: Write a pytest that constructs random fp16 q (shape [1,d]), K,V (shape [block_size, d]) for a single head, invokes the PagedAttention kernel with context_len=block_size and a 1-entry block_table, and asserts torch.allclose(kernel_output, torch.softmax(q@K.T / sqrt(d), -1)@V, atol=1e-3).

sub_tasks.requirements: Unit test: for a multi-block context length (e.g., context_len = 3.5 * block_size, partially filled last block) with randomly scrambled block-table indices into non-contiguous physical blocks, the output matches the reference torch attention within 1e-3 absolute tolerance in fp16.

verification.spec: Write a pytest that constructs random fp16 q, K, V for context_len = 3*block_size + block_size//2 (partial last block), builds a block_table pointing to 4 randomly-permuted non-contiguous physical block ids in a physical KV pool populated accordingly, invokes PagedAttention, and asserts allclose vs. reference torch attention over the full context with atol=1e-3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Unit test: with multiple attention heads (e.g., num_heads = 8) and multi-head KV cache stored as separate physical blocks per head, PagedAttention outputs match the reference multi-head attention within 1e-3 absolute tolerance in fp16.

verification.spec: Unit test: with num_heads=8, head_size=64, block_size=16, allocate KV cache in the paged layout for a sequence of 40 tokens. Compute PagedAttention output for a single query and compare to a reference torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention computed on the un-paged K,V. Assert max abs diff < 1e-3 in fp16.

sub_tasks.requirements: Unit test: with a batch of requests whose context_lens differ (e.g., [17, 65, 128, 4]) all packed against the same block_size, PagedAttention produces per-request outputs each matching the corresponding standard-attention reference within 1e-3 absolute tolerance in fp16.

verification.spec: Unit test: build a batch with context_lens=[17,65,128,4] and block_size=16. For each request, materialize K,V by gathering blocks per its block_table. Invoke PagedAttention once for the batch, and independently compute reference attention per request. Assert per-request max abs diff < 1e-3 in fp16.

sub_tasks.requirements: End-to-end behavioral check: swapping the model's attention op for PagedAttention (with the standard KV cache re-packed into blocks) yields identical greedy-decoding token sequences to the un-paged reference on a fixed prompt (verified against a small toy model).

verification.spec: Instantiate a small toy transformer (e.g., 2 layers, 128 hidden). Run greedy decoding with a reference contiguous-KV attention producing token sequence T_ref. Rewire the model's attention to PagedAttention with block_size=16 and rerun greedy decoding on the same prompt to obtain T_paged. Assert T_ref == T_paged token-for-token.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PagedAttention kernel supports the block-size sweep required by ablation §7.2 and Section 4.3's discussion of block_size > 1 enabling parallelism.

Code has been implemented such that block_size is a compile-time or runtime template parameter accepting each of {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256}, and each variant passes the numerical-equivalence unit test.

verification.spec: For each block_size in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256}, instantiate the PagedAttention kernel (compile-time template or runtime parameter) and run the multi-block numerical-equivalence pytest asserting allclose vs. reference torch attention within 1e-3.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel dispatches per-block work to a GPU warp (32 threads) as described in Section 5.1 ('we assign a GPU warp to read each block'), and the launch grid scales as ceil(context_len / block_size) blocks per (head, request).

verification.spec: Inspect the PagedAttention CUDA/Triton kernel source. Assert (a) thread block is configured such that threads-per-block is a multiple of 32 and each block cooperates on one KV block (warp-per-block), and (b) the grid dimension = (num_heads * batch_size, ceil(max_context_len / block_size)) or equivalent, so grid scales as ceil(context_len/block_size) per (head, request).

sub_tasks.requirements: Behavioral check: increasing block_size from 1 to 16 while keeping context_len fixed reduces the number of block-fetch iterations by 16x, verified by counting per-warp iterations in a debug build.

verification.spec: Instrument the debug build to count per-warp block-fetch iterations (e.g., via an atomic counter passed to the kernel). Run once with block_size=1 and once with block_size=16 for the same 256-token context. Assert count(bs=1) / count(bs=16) is approximately 16 (within ±1).

sub_tasks.requirements: The KV cache manager implements logical-to-physical KV block mapping via block tables (Figure 6), a block engine that reserves contiguous GPU DRAM and partitions it into fixed-size physical KV blocks, and dynamic on-demand allocation as tokens are generated, mirroring the OS virtual-memory analogy in Section 4.2-4.3.
Core data structures for logical/physical KV blocks and block-table entries exist and behave as described in Section 4.2.

Code has been implemented for a `LogicalKVBlock` (or equivalently named) data structure that stores the block size B, a `num_filled` counter, and provides append/space-remaining operations used by the manager.

verification.spec: Import LogicalKVBlock (or equivalent). Instantiate with block_size=B=8. Assert the object has attributes `block_size` (=8), `num_filled` (initial 0), and methods `append(token_id)` and `space_remaining()`. Call append 5 times; assert num_filled==5 and space_remaining()==3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a `PhysicalKVBlock` (or equivalently named) data structure that carries a device tag (GPU/CPU), an integer physical block id, and a reference count field used by the copy-on-write and free logic.

verification.spec: Import PhysicalKVBlock (or equivalent). Instantiate with device='gpu', block_number=7. Assert attributes `device` ('gpu' or enum), `block_number` (int, ==7), and `ref_count` (int, initial 1). Assert the class is used by the copy-on-write path (grep for `ref_count` in COW code).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a `BlockTable` structure that stores, per logical block index, the mapped physical block number and the `#filled` counter shown in Figure 6.

verification.spec: Import BlockTable. Instantiate an empty table, append two physical blocks (numbers 7 and 1). Assert indexing returns (physical_block_number, num_filled) pairs matching Figure 6: e.g., table[0] -> (7, 4), table[1] -> (1, 3) after filling with 7 tokens at block_size=4.

sub_tasks.requirements: The BlockTable append operation only allocates a new physical block when the current last logical block reaches `num_filled == B`; otherwise a token is written into the free slot of the existing last block and `#filled` is incremented by one.

verification.spec: Instantiate a BlockTable with block_size B. Append B-1 tokens; assert exactly 1 physical block was allocated and #filled == B-1. Append one more token; assert still only 1 block allocated and #filled == B. Append one more token; assert a new physical block was allocated (block_count == 2) and the new block's #filled == 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The block engine reserves a contiguous chunk of GPU DRAM (and mirrored CPU RAM) at initialization and partitions it into fixed-size physical KV blocks, as required by Section 4.2 and Figure 4.

Code has been implemented for a `BlockEngine` (or equivalent) that, given a total GPU KV cache byte budget, allocates a single contiguous CUDA tensor and exposes it as an array of physical KV blocks of shape (num_layers, num_heads_per_shard, head_dim, block_size) for keys and values.

verification.spec: Import the BlockEngine (or equivalent) class from src/. Instantiate it with a specified GPU byte budget and model config (num_layers, num_heads, head_dim, block_size). Assert it allocates a single contiguous CUDA tensor per layer for keys and values with shape (num_blocks, num_heads_per_shard, head_dim, block_size), and exposes a view over that tensor as per-block slices.

sub_tasks.requirements: The block engine computes the number of physical GPU KV blocks by profiling remaining free memory after model load minus an activation reserve, dividing by per-block bytes; this determines `num_gpu_blocks` used by the allocator.

verification.spec: After loading a target model into GPU memory, call the block-engine's profiling routine. Verify it (a) queries torch.cuda.mem_get_info() or equivalent to get free bytes, (b) subtracts a configured activation reserve, (c) divides by per-block bytes (computed from num_layers*num_heads*head_dim*block_size*2*dtype_bytes), and (d) sets num_gpu_blocks to that integer. Assert the returned num_gpu_blocks matches this formula.

sub_tasks.requirements: The block engine additionally reserves a CPU-side block pool (see Figure 4) of `num_cpu_blocks` physical blocks with the same shape, used later by the swapping mechanism (§4.5).

verification.spec: Import the block engine; instantiate with a nonzero swap_space_bytes. Assert it allocates a pinned/CPU tensor pool sized to `num_cpu_blocks` blocks with the same per-block shape as the GPU pool, and exposes a CPUBlockAllocator over it.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a `GPUBlockAllocator` and a `CPUBlockAllocator` that maintain free lists of physical block ids and expose `allocate()` returning a fresh block (ref_count=1) and `free(block)` returning it to the free list when ref_count decrements to 0.

verification.spec: Import GPUBlockAllocator and CPUBlockAllocator. For each, allocate N blocks and record ids; assert every returned block starts with ref_count == 1 and ids are unique. Call free() on each; assert the ids return to the free list and subsequent allocations reuse them. Verify allocate() raises or returns None when the free list is exhausted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Calling `allocate()` more than `num_gpu_blocks` times without any intervening `free()` raises an out-of-memory error, so the scheduler can invoke preemption rather than corrupting the pool.

verification.spec: Instantiate GPUBlockAllocator with num_blocks=3. Call allocate() 3 times successfully. Call allocate() a 4th time without any intervening free(); assert it raises an OutOfMemoryError (or vLLM-defined equivalent) rather than returning None or a duplicate block.

sub_tasks.requirements: The KV cache manager (Section 4.2) exposes the block-table mapping between per-request logical blocks and the block-engine physical blocks and coordinates allocation across concurrent sequences (Figure 7).

Code has been implemented for a `KVCacheManager` (or `BlockManager`) that owns the GPU and CPU allocators and stores, per sequence, its `BlockTable` — the sole mapping the rest of the engine consults to locate KV cache.

verification.spec: Import KVCacheManager (or BlockManager). Instantiate it; assert it holds attributes `gpu_allocator` (GPUBlockAllocator instance), `cpu_allocator` (CPUBlockAllocator instance), and a mapping `block_tables: Dict[seq_id, BlockTable]`. Call `allocate(seq)`; assert an entry appears in block_tables[seq.id] and physical blocks came from gpu_allocator.

sub_tasks.requirements: The manager exposes `can_allocate(seq)` returning true iff enough free physical blocks exist to cover ceil(len(prompt)/B) new blocks, used by the scheduler before admitting the request.

verification.spec: Instantiate the KV cache manager with a known number of free blocks F and block size B. Call can_allocate(seq) with prompts of length L such that ceil(L/B) <= F and ceil(L/B) > F; assert True for the first and False for the second. Also verify it returns False after other sequences have consumed enough blocks.

sub_tasks.requirements: The manager exposes `allocate(seq)` which reserves exactly ceil(prompt_len/B) physical blocks and builds an initial block table with `#filled` equal to B for full blocks and `prompt_len mod B` for the last partial block.

verification.spec: Call allocate(seq) on a sequence with prompt_len=10 and B=4. Assert 3 physical blocks are reserved, block table has 3 entries, #filled values are [4,4,2], and free block count decreased by 3. Test edge cases: prompt_len=B (one full block, #filled=B) and prompt_len < B (one block, #filled=prompt_len).

sub_tasks.requirements: The manager exposes `append_slot(seq)` which, when the last logical block has a free slot, only bumps `#filled`, and otherwise allocates a new physical block and appends a new logical-block entry to the table (matching step ○3 in Section 4.3).

verification.spec: Allocate a seq with prompt_len=7, B=4 (last block #filled=3). Call append_slot(seq): assert no new physical block allocated, block table length unchanged, last entry's #filled becomes 4. Call append_slot again: assert a new physical block is allocated, block table grows by 1 entry with #filled=1.

sub_tasks.requirements: The manager exposes `free(seq)` which decrements the ref_count of every physical block referenced by the sequence's block table and returns to the free list any block whose count drops to zero.

verification.spec: Allocate seq1 and seq2 that share zero physical blocks. Call free(seq1), assert all its physical blocks return to free list (free count increases by ceil(len/B)). Then allocate seq3 sharing physical blocks with seq2 (ref_count=2), call free(seq2): assert shared blocks' ref_count decrements to 1 and are NOT returned to free list, while unshared blocks are.

sub_tasks.requirements: The manager exposes `get_block_table(seq)` returning the ordered list of physical block ids used by the attention kernel and (in the distributed case) broadcast by the scheduler each step.

verification.spec: Allocate a sequence and append tokens. Call get_block_table(seq); assert it returns an ordered list/tensor of physical block ids matching the internal mapping (in logical block order). Verify length equals ceil(current_len/B) and the values match those tracked internally.

sub_tasks.requirements: Dynamic on-demand allocation and the Figure 6 walkthrough behavior is faithfully reproduced during prompt and autoregressive decoding steps.

For a 7-token prompt with block size B=4, prompt-phase allocation produces exactly 2 logical blocks whose `#filled` values are [4, 3] and reserves no additional blocks (reproducing step ○1 in Section 4.3).

verification.spec: Set B=4, allocate a sequence with prompt_len=7. Assert len(block_table)==2, #filled == [4,3], and total physical blocks used == 2 (no extra reservation for future tokens). This directly reproduces step 1 of Figure 6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Generating the first output token on the 7/8 prompt above writes into the free slot of the existing last physical block (no new allocation) and updates `#filled` from 3 to 4 (step ○2).

verification.spec: Continuing the B=4, prompt_len=7 setup: record the last physical block id and free block count, then invoke the append/generation step. Assert the last physical block id is unchanged, free block count unchanged, and #filled updated from 3 to 4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Generating the eighth-plus-one token when the last logical block is full triggers allocation of a fresh physical block, appends a new logical block entry with `#filled = 1`, and updates the block table with the new mapping (step ○3).

verification.spec: Continue from previous test with #filled=[4,4]. Trigger generation of the 9th token. Assert block table grows to length 3, new entry #filled==1, and free block count decreased by 1 (a fresh physical block was allocated).

sub_tasks.requirements: The manager never pre-allocates for the model's maximum sequence length; the total physical blocks held by a sequence at any moment equals ceil(current_length / B).

verification.spec: Instrument the manager to record allocated physical blocks per sequence during a decode of arbitrary length up to some N << max_model_len. At every step, assert allocated_blocks(seq) == ceil(current_len/B). Also assert the manager never allocates more than that at any point, regardless of model max_seq_len (e.g., 2048).

sub_tasks.requirements: Two concurrently running sequences (Figure 7) receive disjoint physical block ids drawn from the shared block-engine pool and their logical-block sequences map to interleaved, non-contiguous physical block ids, verified by inspecting both block tables side-by-side after running a two-sequence decode step.

verification.spec: Allocate two independent sequences seqA and seqB from the same block engine, decode a few tokens each interleaved. Extract both block tables; assert (a) set(seqA_blocks) ∩ set(seqB_blocks) == ∅, (b) all ids come from the block engine's pool, and (c) the interleaved ids are not consecutively-numbered (verifying non-contiguous physical layout).

sub_tasks.requirements: When one of the two concurrent sequences finishes and is freed, its physical blocks return to the free list and become allocatable by a subsequently admitted third sequence, verified via free-block-count deltas.

verification.spec: Allocate seqA and seqB, record free_block_count. Free seqA and assert free_block_count increased by ceil(lenA/B). Then admit a new seqC of length lenC; assert allocation succeeds and at least one of seqC's physical block ids was previously held by seqA.

sub_tasks.requirements: Attention/write-side code consumes the block table correctly so that the physical KV blocks the manager returns are the ones actually read and written.

Code has been implemented for a `write_kv` path that, given a per-sequence block table and the new-token position, computes (block_idx = pos // B, offset = pos % B) and writes the new K/V into the corresponding slot of the physical block returned by the manager.

verification.spec: Import the write_kv function. Given a mock block table [p0, p1, p2], call write_kv(pos=6, K=k_tensor, V=v_tensor, B=4). Assert it writes to physical block p1 (since 6//4=1) at offset 2 (since 6%4=2). Repeat for pos=0 (p0, off 0) and pos=11 (p2, off 3).

sub_tasks.requirements: A round-trip test writes a distinguishable K/V tensor at token position p via the manager's mapping and reads it back through the same block-table lookup, recovering the exact tensor (bit-exact for FP16), thereby validating the logical→physical translation end-to-end.

verification.spec: Allocate a sequence of length L with B=4. Generate unique FP16 K/V tensors T_p for each position p, write them via the manager's mapping. Read back all K/V at each p via block_table lookup and assert torch.equal(read, T_p) exactly (bit-exact FP16) for every p in [0, L).

sub_tasks.requirements: The block table sent to workers is represented as a padded int32 tensor of shape (num_seqs, max_logical_blocks) so that the PagedAttention kernel and the fused reshape+write kernel can index it directly, matching the interface described in §5.1.

verification.spec: Prepare a batch of sequences of different logical-block counts. Call the scheduler's build_block_tables (or equivalent) that produces the worker-broadcast tensor. Assert dtype==torch.int32, shape==(num_seqs, max_logical_blocks), padded entries are a sentinel (e.g., 0 or -1), and non-padded entries match get_block_table(seq).

sub_tasks.requirements: Numerical claim: the block-level manager achieves near-zero waste — memory waste per request is bounded to at most one block, so effective KV-cache utilization matches the vLLM bar in Figure 2 (~96.3% token-state utilization) rather than the 20.4-38.2% range of the Orca baselines.

Instrumentation exists that, given a completed workload, sums per-sequence (allocated_blocks * B - actual_tokens) and divides by total allocated slots to report the KV-cache internal-fragmentation fraction, and reports zero reserved/external fragmentation for vLLM.

verification.spec: Run a synthetic workload of N completed sequences with known (allocated_blocks_i, actual_tokens_i). Call the reporting function; assert it returns internal_frag == sum(alloc*B - tokens)/sum(alloc*B), reserved_frag == 0, and external_frag == 0 for vLLM. Verify numeric correctness on a hand-computed example.

sub_tasks.requirements: On the §6.2 ShareGPT OPT-13B trace, the measured token-state fraction of allocated KV-cache slots for vLLM matches the Figure 2 vLLM bar of approximately 96.3% (within tolerance), demonstrating that per-request waste is at most one partially filled block.

verification.spec: Run vLLM on the ShareGPT trace with OPT-13B (or a smaller stand-in if 13B unavailable, e.g., OPT-1.3B/facebook/opt-1.3b with the same trace and B=16). Run the fragmentation instrumentation; assert token-state fraction of allocated KV slots is within tolerance of 96.3%.

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM supports parallel sampling with copy-on-write physical block sharing, beam search with dynamic block sharing across candidates, shared-prefix caching, and mixed decoding via fork/append/free primitives (Section 4.4, 5.2, Figures 8-10).
vLLM exposes three sequence-manipulation primitives — fork, append, free — that all complex decoding algorithms (parallel sampling, beam search, prefix sharing) are composed from (Section 5.2).

Code has been implemented for a fork(seq_id) method on the sequence/scheduler that creates a new sequence sharing the parent sequence's existing KV blocks (with reference counts incremented on the shared physical blocks).

verification.spec: Allocate a parent sequence with prompt of length L. Record ref counts of its physical blocks. Call fork(parent_id) to get child_id; assert (a) child.block_table == parent.block_table (same physical ids), (b) each parent physical block's ref_count incremented by 1, (c) no new physical blocks allocated.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for an append(seq_id, token) method that appends a newly generated token's KV cache to the sequence's last logical block, allocating a new physical block if the last block is full.

verification.spec: Allocate a seq with a non-full last block. Call append(seq_id, token_id); assert last block's #filled increased by 1 and no new physical block allocated. Fill the last block, call append again; assert a new physical block is allocated and the block table grew by 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a free(seq_id) method that deletes a sequence, decrementing the reference counts of its physical blocks and returning any physical block whose reference count reaches zero to the free-block pool.

verification.spec: Allocate seq with L tokens (ceil(L/B) blocks, all ref_count=1). Call free(seq_id); assert seq is removed from tracked sequences and all its physical blocks returned to free pool (free_count increased by ceil(L/B)). Test also that shared blocks (ref>1) are NOT returned but ref_count decremented.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test demonstrates that parallel sampling, beam search, and prefix-sharing paths in the codebase are each implemented by combining only fork/append/free primitives (no bespoke sequence-management code paths for each decoding mode).

verification.spec: Statically parse the source of the parallel_sampling, beam_search, and shared_prefix implementations (via ast). Assert that inside each function's call graph, sequence management operations are limited to calls named fork, append, and free (plus the read-only get_block_table / can_allocate). Assert no direct manipulation of physical block ids or ref_counts inside these three code paths.

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM supports parallel sampling: a single request produces multiple output samples that share the prompt's KV cache via physical block sharing with reference counting and a copy-on-write mechanism at block granularity (Section 4.4, Figure 8).
Code has been implemented so that a request with N parallel samples generates N output sequences from one input prompt, and only one copy of the prompt's KV cache is materialized at the prompt phase.

verification.spec: Issue a request with N=4 parallel samples and prompt of length P (P > B). Instrument physical-block allocations during the prompt phase; assert exactly ceil(P/B) physical blocks are materialized (not 4*ceil(P/B)). Then assert 4 output sequences are produced.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that at the prompt phase in parallel sampling, all sample sequences' logical prompt blocks map to the SAME physical blocks (i.e., logical block 0/1 of both samples in Figure 8 both point to physical blocks 7 and 1).

verification.spec: Issue a parallel sampling request N=2, prompt_len=7, B=4 (mirroring Figure 8). Fetch block_table(sampleA) and block_table(sampleB); assert both are the same list of physical block ids for the prompt-covering logical blocks (block 0 and block 1 map to identical physical ids across A and B).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a per-physical-block reference count on the physical KV block allocator; the count is incremented every time an additional logical block maps to the physical block.

verification.spec: Access the physical block allocator; assert each PhysicalBlock has a ref_count attribute (or the allocator maintains a ref_count table). Allocate a block: ref_count == 1. Fork a sequence to make an additional logical block map to it: assert ref_count == 2. Fork again: ref_count == 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that after forking N samples from a prompt of length P (with block size B), each physical block covering the prompt has reference count N and the total physical blocks used equals ceil(P/B) (not N * ceil(P/B)).

verification.spec: Set N=4, P=12, B=4 → ceil(P/B)=3. Allocate parent, fork 3 additional samples. Record free_block_count before/after. Assert (a) free_block_count decreased by exactly 3 (not 12), (b) each of the 3 prompt-covering physical blocks has ref_count == 4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for a copy-on-write mechanism at block granularity: when a sample writes to a physical block whose reference count > 1, the block allocator allocates a new physical block, copies data from the old block, redirects the writing sample's logical block, and decrements the old block's reference count.

verification.spec: Set up a shared physical block P with ref_count=2, mapped by logical block 1 of both sampleA and sampleB. Perform a write on behalf of sampleA to a position within P. Assert (a) a new physical block P' was allocated, (b) contents of P were copied to P', (c) sampleA's logical block 1 now maps to P', (d) P's ref_count decremented to 1, (e) sampleB's mapping is unchanged.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test reproduces the Figure 8 scenario: with two samples sharing physical block 1 (ref_count=2), when sample A1 writes 'mothers' to its last logical block, a new physical block (analogue of block 3) is allocated and the original block's ref_count is decremented to 1.

verification.spec: Instantiate the block manager with two logical sequences sharing physical block 1 (ref_count=2). Invoke the write path for sample A1 appending a new token 'mothers' to its last logical block. Assert (a) a new physical block is allocated for A1's last logical block, (b) A1's block-table now points to that new block, (c) the original physical block 1's ref_count is decremented to 1, and (d) sample A2's block-table still references the original physical block 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that after a COW event decrements a shared block's ref_count to 1, the next sample writing to that same physical block performs a direct in-place write (no additional copy is performed).

verification.spec: Set up a physical block with ref_count=1 (simulating the state after a prior COW event). Have another sample write a new token that lands on that block. Assert that no new physical block is allocated (block-allocator's allocate() is not called), the write is performed in place into the existing physical block, and ref_count remains 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: for parallel sampling on OPT-13B with the Alpaca trace, the average KV-block memory savings (blocks saved via sharing / total blocks without sharing) fall in the range 6.1%-9.8% across sample counts of 2, 4, and 6 (Figure 15a).

verification.spec: Run vLLM's parallel-sampling workload on OPT-13B with the Alpaca trace at sample counts N=2, 4, 6. For each N, log total KV blocks allocated with sharing enabled vs. total that would have been required without sharing (N * per-sequence blocks). Compute savings ratio = 1 - (with_sharing / without_sharing). Assert all three values fall inside [0.061, 0.098].

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: for parallel sampling on OPT-13B with the ShareGPT trace, the average KV-block memory savings fall in the range 16.2%-30.5% across sample counts of 2, 4, and 6 (Section 6.3).

verification.spec: Run vLLM's parallel-sampling workload on OPT-13B with the ShareGPT trace at sample counts N=2, 4, 6. For each N, compute KV-block sharing savings = 1 - (blocks_with_sharing / blocks_without_sharing). Assert all three values fall inside [0.162, 0.305].

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM supports beam search with a beam-width parameter k, dynamic block sharing across beam candidates whose sharing pattern evolves with the decoding process, all-or-nothing gang-scheduling of the beam candidates as one sequence group, and reference-count-driven freeing of pruned candidates' blocks (Section 4.4, Figure 9).
Code has been implemented for a configurable beam_width parameter k passed through the sampling parameters API, controlling how many top candidates are retained each decoding step.

verification.spec: Import the SamplingParams / request-config type and construct instances with beam_width values 1, 2, 4, 6. Submit each to the engine and verify: (a) the parameter is accepted and stored, (b) at each decoding step for beam_width=k the scheduler tracks exactly k live candidate sequences per request until termination.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for the beam-search selection step that, from each of k candidate sequences extended by all |V| possible tokens, retains the top-k highest-probability continuations out of the k*|V| candidates.

verification.spec: Mock/stub the LLM to return a deterministic logits tensor over a small vocabulary V for each of k active beam candidates. Invoke the beam-selection routine. Assert that (a) the candidate pool considered has size k*|V|, and (b) exactly the top-k highest-summed-log-prob continuations (by construction) are retained; verify by comparing against a reference numpy top-k over the flattened k*|V| score matrix.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a new beam candidate is derived by extending a parent candidate, it forks the parent (sharing all of the parent's physical KV blocks with incremented reference counts) rather than deep-copying the KV cache.

verification.spec: Create a parent beam sequence with N physical KV blocks allocated. Fork k child candidates from it via the beam-search machinery. Assert (a) no new physical blocks were allocated for the shared portion (block-allocator.allocate() call-count unchanged), (b) each child's block-table references the same N physical block IDs, and (c) each of those physical blocks has ref_count == k+1 (or k if parent released).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test reproduces the Figure 9 configuration at the pre-iteration snapshot: 4 beam candidates all share block 0 (prompt); candidate 3 diverges from the second block; candidates 0-2 share the first 3 blocks and diverge at the fourth block.

verification.spec: Programmatically drive the beam manager to the Figure 9 pre-iteration state by injecting a sequence of forks/writes that yields 4 beam candidates. Assert: (a) all four candidates' first logical block maps to the same physical block (prompt); (b) candidate 3's second logical block maps to a different physical block than candidates 0-2; (c) candidates 0-2 share physical blocks for logical positions 0, 1, 2 but diverge at logical block 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test reproduces the Figure 9 post-iteration behavior: when the new top-4 candidates all originate from prior candidates 1 and 2, physical blocks whose reference count reaches 0 (the equivalents of blocks 2, 4, 5, 8) are freed and new physical blocks (equivalents of blocks 9-12) are allocated for the new candidates.

verification.spec: Starting from the Figure 9 pre-iteration state, drive one beam-search step where the top-4 new candidates are all derived from prior candidates 1 and 2. Assert: (a) physical blocks previously exclusively held by candidates 0 and 3 (those whose ref_count reaches 0) are returned to the free pool via allocator.free(); (b) 4 new physical blocks are allocated to hold the newly generated KV cache for the 4 new candidates; (c) the surviving shared blocks retain expected ref_counts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that beam candidates within a single beam-search request form a sequence group that is gang-scheduled: the scheduler always preempts or reschedules all beam candidates in a group together (never a strict subset).

verification.spec: Submit a beam-search request (k=4) plus enough concurrent requests to exhaust GPU KV blocks so preemption triggers. Inspect the scheduler's preemption decisions: assert that whenever any candidate of the beam-search request is preempted, all k candidates in the sequence group are preempted in the same scheduling step, and on rescheduling all k are brought back together.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test confirms that when a beam-search sequence group is preempted, all k candidates are evicted together and, upon rescheduling, all k candidates are brought back together.

verification.spec: Set up a beam sequence group of k=4 candidates. Force the scheduler to preempt the group (e.g., by consuming all free blocks). Assert (a) preempt() is called for all 4 candidates, and (b) at the next scheduling step where blocks become free, resume() is invoked for exactly the same 4 candidates atomically (no candidate resumes before the others).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that during beam-search decoding, copy-on-write is applied only when a candidate writes a newly generated token into a still-shared block, and the copy involves exactly one block (not the entire candidate's KV cache).

verification.spec: Configure a beam-search state where the last logical block of candidate A is shared (ref_count > 1) with another candidate B. Have A append a token. Assert (a) exactly one new physical block is allocated (not multiple, not the full candidate KV chain), (b) the block-copy kernel is invoked on exactly one block, and (c) if the last logical block had ref_count == 1, no allocation or copy occurs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: for beam search on OPT-13B with the Alpaca trace, the average KV-block memory savings fall in the range 37.6%-55.2% across beam widths 2, 4, and 6 (Figure 15b).

verification.spec: Run vLLM beam-search on OPT-13B with the Alpaca trace at beam widths k=2, 4, 6. For each k, compute KV-block sharing savings = 1 - (blocks_with_sharing / blocks_without_sharing). Assert all three values fall inside [0.376, 0.552].

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: for beam search on OPT-13B with the ShareGPT trace, the average KV-block memory savings fall in the range 44.3%-66.3% across beam widths 2, 4, and 6 (Section 6.3).

verification.spec: Run vLLM beam-search on OPT-13B with the ShareGPT trace at beam widths k=2, 4, 6. For each k, compute KV-block sharing savings = 1 - (blocks_with_sharing / blocks_without_sharing). Assert all three values fall inside [0.443, 0.663].

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM supports shared-prefix caching: the service provider pre-registers physical blocks for common prefixes (system prompts / few-shot examples), and per-request logical blocks map to those cached physical blocks with the last shared block marked copy-on-write, so the prompt-phase computation runs only on the task-input tokens (Section 4.4, Figure 10).

Code has been implemented for an API that lets the LLM service provider register one or more predefined shared-prefix token sequences and materialize their KV cache into a reserved set of physical blocks that persist across requests.

verification.spec: Import the shared-prefix registration API (e.g., register_shared_prefix(prefix_token_ids)). Register one or more prefixes and verify (a) the API accepts the token id sequence, (b) after registration a set of reserved physical blocks holds the prefix's KV cache, and (c) these blocks are excluded from the free-list used for ordinary requests and persist across multiple request lifecycles.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a request's input prompt starts with a registered shared prefix, the corresponding logical KV blocks are mapped directly to the cached physical blocks (with reference counts incremented) instead of being recomputed.

verification.spec: Register a shared prefix, then submit a request whose input tokens begin with that prefix. Assert (a) the logical KV blocks covering the prefix map to the cached physical block IDs (verify via block-table inspection), (b) the reference counts of those physical blocks are incremented by 1, and (c) no new physical blocks are allocated for the prefix portion (only for the task-specific suffix).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the last logical block that spans the shared prefix is marked copy-on-write, so that writes attempting to modify it trigger the same COW path used by parallel sampling.

verification.spec: Register a shared prefix and submit a request whose input tokens include that prefix followed by additional task-input tokens. Inspect the block-table entry for the last logical block spanning the prefix boundary and assert it is flagged copy-on-write. Then trigger a write to that last logical block and assert the COW path allocates a new physical block, mirroring the parallel-sampling COW mechanism.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the prompt-phase forward pass for a request with a shared prefix computes attention only over the task-input tokens (the prefix tokens' KV cache is read from the cached blocks, not recomputed).

verification.spec: Register a prefix of length P tokens. Submit a request with prefix + T task-input tokens. Instrument the prompt-phase attention/QKV projection call to record the number of query positions computed. Assert exactly T positions are computed (not P+T), while the K/V for prefix positions are read from the reserved cached blocks rather than recomputed.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that serving two requests with the same registered shared prefix causes the prefix's KV cache to be computed exactly once, while the task-input KV cache is computed independently per request.

verification.spec: Register a shared prefix P. Instrument the QKV-projection kernel with a call-counter that records the number of prefix-token KV cache computations. Submit two concurrent requests both starting with prefix P and different task inputs. Assert (a) the prefix KV cache is computed exactly once (call-counter for prefix tokens == P once total, from registration), and (b) each request independently computes KV cache for its own task-input tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: on the WMT16 English-to-German translation workload using LLaMA-13B with a 1-shot (80-token) shared prefix, vLLM sustains ~1.67x higher throughput than Orca (Oracle) (Figure 16a).

verification.spec: Run WMT16 En->De translation workload with LLaMA-13B using a 1-shot (~80-token) shared prefix on both vLLM and the implemented Orca (Oracle) baseline. Sweep request rates and identify the maximum sustained rate per system where normalized latency stays below the paper's threshold. Compute throughput_ratio = vLLM_max_rate / Orca_Oracle_max_rate. Assert the ratio lies within [1.47, 1.87].

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured: on the WMT16 English-to-German translation workload using LLaMA-13B with a 5-shot (341-token) shared prefix, vLLM sustains ~3.58x higher throughput than Orca (Oracle) (Figure 16b).

verification.spec: Run WMT16 En->De translation workload with LLaMA-13B using a 5-shot (~341-token) shared prefix on both vLLM and the implemented Orca (Oracle) baseline. Sweep request rates and compute throughput_ratio = vLLM_max_sustained_rate / Orca_Oracle_max_sustained_rate. Assert the ratio lies within [3.18, 3.98].

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM supports mixed decoding methods: requests using different decoding preferences (basic sampling, parallel sampling, beam search, prefix-shared) can be batched together in a single iteration, because a common logical-to-physical block-mapping layer conceals per-sequence sharing from the model kernels (Section 4.4).

Code has been implemented so that the scheduler can co-batch, in one decoding iteration, requests whose sampling parameters differ across (basic sampling, parallel sampling with N>1, beam search with k>1, shared-prefix requests) without requiring separate execution passes per decoding mode.

verification.spec: Submit a batch containing (i) a basic-sampling request, (ii) a parallel-sampling request with N=4, (iii) a beam-search request with k=4, and (iv) a shared-prefix request in the same iteration. Assert (a) the scheduler places all of them into a single execution pass (one call to the model executor), (b) the executor's forward is invoked exactly once for that iteration, and (c) all requests advance by one token.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the model executor / attention kernel receives only a flat list of physical block IDs per sequence and is oblivious to which sequences share which blocks — the sharing pattern lives entirely in the block-table mapping layer above the kernel.

verification.spec: Inspect the model-executor / attention-kernel call signature and confirm it accepts only per-sequence flat physical block-ID lists (e.g., an int[num_seqs, max_blocks] tensor) plus sequence metadata. Assert the kernel signature contains no arguments naming reference counts, shared-block flags, or copy-on-write state. Grep the kernel source (e.g., csrc/attention*.cu) for identifiers like 'ref_count', 'shared', 'cow' and assert none appear.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test constructs a batch containing at least one basic-sampling request, one parallel-sampling request, one beam-search request, and one shared-prefix request, and verifies that a single forward pass produces correct outputs for all of them.

verification.spec: Build a batch with four requests: basic sampling (N=1), parallel sampling (N=3), beam search (k=3), shared-prefix (with a registered prefix). Run one forward pass. Compare each request's output logits/tokens to those produced by running the same requests one-at-a-time; assert bitwise-equivalent tokens (or within numerical tolerance for softmax) for all four requests.

depends_on: KV Cache Manager & Block Table Translation

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM's FCFS scheduler with all-or-nothing eviction, sequence-group gang-scheduling, and both swapping (to CPU RAM via CPU block allocator) and recomputation preemption/recovery mechanisms are implemented as described in Section 4.5.
A first-come-first-serve (FCFS) scheduler prioritizes earlier-arrived requests during admission and preemption to prevent starvation.

Code has been implemented defining a Scheduler class/module that maintains a waiting queue of requests ordered by arrival timestamp and exposes a step()/schedule() entry point invoked once per decoding iteration.

verification.spec: Use importlib to import the Scheduler module and assert (a) a Scheduler class is defined, (b) it has a step()/schedule() method invoked per decoding iteration, and (c) its state includes a waiting queue ordered by arrival timestamp (verify by inserting several dummy requests with out-of-order timestamps and calling the sort/dequeue path, then asserting FCFS order out).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that at admission time the scheduler pops requests from the waiting queue in strict arrival-time order (FCFS); a unit test injecting requests with monotonically increasing arrival times observes them scheduled in the same order.

verification.spec: Instantiate the scheduler and enqueue 5 requests with monotonically increasing arrival_time (t=1..5) into the waiting queue. Trigger one scheduler admission step under conditions where all can be admitted (or step through admissions). Record the order in which requests transition from WAITING to RUNNING; assert this order equals the arrival-time order (FCFS).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when preemption is required the scheduler selects victim sequences in reverse arrival order (latest-arrived preempted first, earliest-arrived preempted last); a unit test with a running batch of known arrival order verifies the preemption victim is the latest.

verification.spec: Construct a running batch of 4 SequenceGroups with known distinct arrival_time values (t=1,2,3,4). Reduce free GPU block count to force preemption of exactly one group. Call the scheduler step; assert the group with arrival_time=4 (latest) is the one moved to preempted/swapped state and the group with arrival_time=1 remains running.

sub_tasks.requirements: vLLM groups the sequences generated by a single request (e.g., beam candidates, parallel samples) into a SequenceGroup that is gang-scheduled — all sequences in the group are preempted or rescheduled together.
Code has been implemented defining a SequenceGroup (or equivalent) data structure that holds a list of Sequence objects belonging to one request and shares a common request identifier.

verification.spec: Import the SequenceGroup (or equivalently named) class from the implementation. Instantiate with a request_id and a list of 3 Sequence objects. Assert: (a) the class exposes an attribute/method returning the list of Sequence objects, (b) all sequences report the same request/group id, (c) the group length equals 3.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when the scheduler preempts a request, every un-finished sequence in its SequenceGroup is preempted in the same scheduler step; a unit test with a beam-search-style group of 4 sequences confirms all 4 transition to preempted state atomically.

verification.spec: Build a SequenceGroup with 4 unfinished sequences (beam-search style). Configure the scheduler so this group is chosen for preemption in a single step. Invoke the scheduler; assert that after that single step all 4 sequences report a preempted/swapped status (none remain RUNNING), demonstrating atomic gang preemption.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a preempted SequenceGroup is rescheduled, all its constituent sequences are resumed together in the same scheduler step; a unit test verifies partial-group resumption is not permitted.

verification.spec: Preempt a SequenceGroup of 3 sequences, then free enough GPU blocks so the group can be rescheduled. Run one scheduler step; assert all 3 sequences transition to RUNNING in the same step. Additionally attempt (via API or by inspecting the resume routine) to resume only 1 sequence of the group; assert this raises or is not supported.

sub_tasks.requirements: An all-or-nothing eviction policy ensures that either all KV blocks of a sequence are evicted or none are, exploiting the fact that all blocks of a sequence are accessed together.

Code has been implemented providing an eviction routine (e.g., preempt_sequence / evict_sequence) whose input is a Sequence handle and whose effect is to release/swap the full block-table entry list for that sequence.

verification.spec: Locate the eviction/preemption routine (e.g., scheduler.preempt(seq) or block_manager.swap_out(seq)). Populate a Sequence with N (>1) block-table entries. Invoke the routine; assert all N block-table entries are released or moved (GPU block count for the sequence drops to 0, or blocks are marked as swapped). Assert the routine signature accepts a Sequence/SequenceGroup handle.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that a partial-eviction path (evicting only some blocks of a sequence while keeping the sequence in GPU memory) is not exposed as a public API; a behavioral test asserts that after eviction the sequence's GPU block count is exactly zero.

verification.spec: Create a Sequence with 4 allocated GPU KV blocks. Call the eviction/preempt API for that sequence. Query the block manager for GPU blocks held by the sequence; assert count == 0. Additionally inspect the public API surface (dir()/module symbols) and assert no partial-eviction function (e.g., 'evict_some_blocks', 'partial_free') is exported.

sub_tasks.requirements: Swapping preemption copies evicted KV blocks to a CPU block allocator backing GPU-shape blocks in pinned CPU RAM, with the constraints described in Section 4.5.

Code has been implemented defining a CPUBlockAllocator (or equivalently named) class that manages a pool of physical KV blocks residing in pinned CPU memory with the same block size as the GPU allocator.

verification.spec: Import CPUBlockAllocator (or equivalent) and construct it with a given block_size and num_blocks. Assert: (a) block_size attribute equals the value passed and equals the GPU allocator's block size, (b) allocated blocks reside in pinned/host memory (e.g., torch tensor with device=='cpu' and is_pinned() True, or documented pinned pool), (c) allocate()/free() methods exist.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that a swap_out(seq_group) call allocates one CPU block per GPU block held by the group, issues a device-to-host copy of the KV cache contents, updates block-table mappings to point to the CPU blocks, and frees the underlying GPU blocks.

verification.spec: Create a SequenceGroup with G GPU blocks holding known KV cache values. Call swap_out(seq_group). Assert: (1) CPU allocator's used-block count increased by G, (2) block-table entries now reference CPU block IDs, (3) the CPU-side block contents equal the pre-swap GPU contents (via a d2h read-back), (4) the GPU allocator's free-block count increased by G.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that a swap_in(seq_group) call allocates GPU blocks, issues a host-to-device copy from the CPU-side blocks, updates the block table to the new GPU block IDs, and releases the CPU blocks back to the CPU allocator.

verification.spec: Take a SequenceGroup that has been previously swapped_out (G CPU blocks with known contents). Call swap_in(seq_group). Assert: (1) GPU allocator's used-block count increased by G, (2) block-table entries now reference GPU block IDs, (3) the GPU-side block contents equal the pre-swap-out values (round-trip integrity), (4) CPU allocator's free-block count increased by G.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that once any sequence has been swapped out, the scheduler stops admitting new requests from the waiting queue and only resumes admission after every preempted sequence has been swapped back in or completed; a unit test confirms new requests remain in the waiting queue while a swap-out is outstanding.

verification.spec: Set up a scheduler with a running batch, force preemption of at least one sequence via swap_out. Enqueue a new request into the waiting queue. Run one scheduler step; assert the new request remains WAITING (not admitted). Then complete/swap-in all preempted sequences; run another step; assert the new request is now admitted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the CPU block pool is sized to at most the number of GPU KV blocks (i.e., swap space bounded by GPU KV cache capacity), matching the invariant stated in Section 4.5; a unit test asserts the CPU allocator's capacity is initialized from the GPU allocator's block count.

verification.spec: Instantiate the block manager / cache engine with num_gpu_blocks=N and (default or configured) swap_space that yields CPU capacity C. Assert C <= N (or that C is derived from num_gpu_blocks and a bytes-per-block factor consistent with N). Also verify via a getter (e.g., cpu_allocator.num_blocks) that the CPU pool size is initialized to at most N.

sub_tasks.requirements: Recomputation preemption discards the KV blocks of the victim sequence(s) and, upon rescheduling, regenerates the KV cache by re-running a single prompt-phase forward on prompt+already-generated tokens.

Code has been implemented providing a recomputation preemption path that, on preempt, frees all KV blocks of the sequence(s) in the group without any CPU copy and marks the sequences as awaiting recompute.

verification.spec: Configure the scheduler in RECOMPUTE preemption mode. Construct a SequenceGroup with G allocated GPU blocks. Trigger preemption. Assert: (a) all G GPU blocks were freed (GPU allocator's free-block count increased by G), (b) CPU allocator's used-block count is unchanged (zero d2h copies), (c) the sequence's status is set to a 'waiting-for-recompute' / 'swapped-recompute' state.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that when a recompute-preempted sequence is rescheduled, its new input token list is the concatenation of the original prompt tokens and all tokens generated before preemption, and the KV cache for the entire concatenated context is regenerated in one prompt-phase iteration (not step-by-step).

verification.spec: Preempt (recompute mode) a sequence that has original prompt tokens P (len=n) and generated tokens G (len=m). On resume, intercept the input token IDs fed into the model's prompt-phase forward call and assert (a) the input length equals n+m and equals concat(P, G), (b) the forward is invoked only once (one prompt-phase iteration) rather than m+1 decoding iterations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that after a recompute cycle the sequence's next generated token is identical (up to sampling seed) to what it would have generated without preemption; a unit test with greedy sampling and a fixed prompt/output prefix confirms deterministic continuation.

verification.spec: With greedy sampling (temperature=0) and a fixed prompt, run the engine to completion without preemption and record the output token sequence O_ref. Then rerun with the same prompt but force at least one recompute-preemption at a middle decoding step; record the output O_test. Assert O_test == O_ref up to the maximum output length.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler triggers preemption exactly when the GPU physical block pool cannot fit the KV blocks required by the running batch's next step, and exposes a configuration knob to select between swapping and recomputation as the recovery mode.

Code has been implemented so that at each scheduler step, if the sum of blocks required by the running SequenceGroups exceeds free GPU blocks, preemption is invoked until the running batch fits or the batch is empty; a unit test that saturates the block pool observes preemption being invoked.

verification.spec: Instrument the scheduler's preemption routine with a call counter. Populate a running batch such that sum(required_blocks) > free GPU blocks. Run one scheduler step; assert preemption was invoked >=1 times and that after the step either the running batch fits in free blocks or the running batch is empty.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented exposing a scheduler / engine configuration flag (e.g., swap_space or preemption_mode) that selects between SWAP and RECOMPUTE recovery paths, defaulting per Section 4.5; a unit test toggles both modes and observes the corresponding code path is exercised.

verification.spec: Locate the config flag (e.g., preemption_mode / swap_space). Instantiate the engine twice: once with SWAP mode, once with RECOMPUTE mode. In each configuration, force a preemption and monkey-patch swap_out and recompute-preempt to record which path was invoked. Assert SWAP mode invokes swap_out (and not the recompute path) and RECOMPUTE mode invokes the recompute path (and not swap_out).

sub_tasks.requirements: End-to-end preempt-and-resume correctness: sequences that go through a full preempt->swap-out->swap-in cycle (or preempt->recompute cycle) resume and produce a valid completion.

A behavioral test that submits N requests exceeding aggregate GPU KV capacity under the SWAP recovery mode completes all requests successfully, with each completed sequence's output matching the output produced by an un-preempted single-request run of the same prompt (greedy sampling, fixed seed).

verification.spec: With a small model (e.g., OPT-125M), configure a tiny KV cache pool so that N>=8 concurrent requests exceed aggregate GPU capacity. Run first with SWAP recovery mode using greedy sampling and fixed seed; record each request's output. Independently generate a reference output by running each prompt alone (no contention). verification.spec: Run the paged_attention_v1 kernel with block_size=16 under `ncu --metrics smsp__warps_launched.sum,l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld.sum`; parse output; assert warps_per_block = 1 (i.e., total warps launched / (num_blocks * num_heads * batch) == 1) within tolerance 0.25.
verification.paper_cite: Section 5.1 (2) 'we assign a GPU warp to read each block'
